screening_decisions.reason: This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in elderly adults, but the outcomes assessed are influenza efficacy, immunogenicity, and safety only. No cardiovascular death or cardiovascular events were measured.
This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in elderly people, but outcomes are limited to serological and clinical influenza incidence. No cardiovascular outcomes were assessed.
This is an RCT of H5N1 prepandemic vaccine vs placebo, but outcomes are immunogenicity, cross-reactivity, and safety. No cardiovascular death or events were assessed.

This is a PROBE study (prospective randomized open with blinded endpoint) comparing influenza vaccine vs no treatment in patients with acute coronary syndrome (CVD population). The primary endpoint was combined major cardiovascular events including death, hospitalization from ACS, heart failure, and stroke. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT evaluating immunogenicity and safety of H1N1 vaccines. Outcomes are seroprotection rates and adverse reactions. No cardiovascular outcomes were assessed.
This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in healthy elderly people, but outcomes are influenza frequency and cost-effectiveness indicators. No cardiovascular death or events were assessed.

This is a substudy of an RCT focusing on humoral immune response (antibody levels) in patients with coronary artery disease. While the parent study may have assessed cardiovascular outcomes, this substudy only reports immunogenicity data.
This is an observational prospective study using administrative database data, not an RCT. Although it mentions cardiac failure outcomes, the study design does not meet the RCT requirement.
This is an RCT comparing intranasal vs intramuscular influenza vaccine formulations in healthy adults. Outcomes are immunogenicity and adverse events. No cardiovascular outcomes were assessed.
This is an RCT comparing high-dose vs standard-dose influenza vaccine in elderly adults. Outcomes are safety, immunogenicity, and influenza efficacy. No cardiovascular death or events were assessed.
This is an RCT primarily evaluating RSV vaccines given with influenza vaccine. Outcomes are humoral responses to RSV and influenza. No cardiovascular death or events were assessed.

This is a single-blind controlled study (not fully randomized) investigating vaccine effects on warfarin anticoagulation. Outcomes are INR values and anticoagulant control. No cardiovascular death or events were assessed.
This is a before-after experimental study with a control group, not an RCT. It evaluates vaccination campaign strategies and coverage rates, not cardiovascular outcomes from vaccination.
This is a case-control study (370 stroke patients vs 370 controls), not an RCT. Although it assesses stroke risk, the study design does not meet the RCT requirement.

This is a prospective randomized study (single-blind) comparing influenza vaccine vs control in myocardial infarction patients and PCI patients (CVD population). Primary outcomes include cardiovascular death and composite ischemic events. Meets all selection criteria.

This is an ecological/comparative study comparing vaccination programs across municipalities, not an RCT. Although it mentions cardiovascular hospitalizations, the study design does not meet the RCT requirement.

This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in elderly persons, but primary outcomes are immunogenicity (seroprotection rates, GMTs). While unplanned hospital admissions were reported, they were not specifically cardiovascular events.

This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in patients on warfarin, but primary outcomes are INR values and warfarin dose stability. Minor bleeding events were noted but these are not cardiovascular death or non-fatal cardiovascular events as defined in the protocol.

This is an RCT evaluating safety/tolerability of FluMist plus TIV vs placebo plus TIV in seniors with chronic conditions. Outcomes are reactogenicity and safety only. No cardiovascular death or events were assessed.

Despite the title suggesting relevance, the abstract describes this as a meta-analysis methods paper teaching systematic review procedures. It is not an RCT and contains no primary data on influenza vaccination and cardiovascular outcomes.

This is an RCT of influenza vaccine vs placebo in healthy adults. However, the outcomes assessed are influenza illness, fever, and respiratory symptoms - NOT cardiovascular death or non-fatal cardiovascular events. Does not meet outcome criteria.
This is an RCT of influenza vaccine dosing in patients with haematological malignancies. Outcomes are immune response (antibody titers) - NOT cardiovascular outcomes. Does not meet outcome criteria.

This is a review article discussing the biologic basis and epidemiologic evidence for a relationship between influenza and cardiovascular disease. It is NOT a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet study design criteria.

This is an RCT comparing two influenza vaccines in elderly people. Outcomes are influenza infection prevention - NOT cardiovascular death or non-fatal cardiovascular events. Does not meet outcome criteria.

This is an RCT comparing concomitant vs sequential administration of Tdap and influenza vaccines. Outcomes are safety, immunogenicity, and adverse events - NOT cardiovascular outcomes. Does not meet outcome criteria.
This is an RCT comparing two influenza vaccine formulations. Outcomes are safety, reactogenicity, and antibody titers - NOT cardiovascular outcomes. Does not meet outcome criteria.

This is an RCT of LAIV vs placebo in healthy working adults. Outcomes are febrile illness, work loss, and health care use - NOT cardiovascular death or non-fatal cardiovascular events. Does not meet outcome criteria.
This is an RCT comparing inactivated vs live attenuated influenza vaccines. Outcomes are laboratory-confirmed influenza illness - NOT cardiovascular outcomes. Does not meet outcome criteria.
This is an RCT comparing cell culture-derived vs egg-based influenza vaccines. Outcomes are safety, reactogenicity, and immunogenicity - NOT cardiovascular outcomes. Does not meet outcome criteria.
This is an RCT assessing oculorespiratory symptoms after influenza vaccination. Outcomes are ocular and respiratory symptoms - NOT cardiovascular outcomes. Does not meet outcome criteria.

This is an RCT assessing safety and immunogenicity of influenza vaccine in adults previously vaccinated. Outcomes are adverse events and antibody titers - NOT cardiovascular outcomes. Does not meet outcome criteria.
This is an RCT evaluating concomitant administration of PCV13 and influenza vaccine. Outcomes are immunogenicity and safety - NOT cardiovascular outcomes. Does not meet outcome criteria.
This is an RCT of H1N1 vaccine in various age groups. Outcomes are safety and immunogenicity (serologic analysis) - NOT cardiovascular outcomes. Does not meet outcome criteria.

This is an RCT comparing concomitant vs sequential administration of Tdap-IPV and influenza vaccine. Outcomes are antibody titres and adverse events - NOT cardiovascular outcomes. Does not meet outcome criteria.
This is a policy/guidance document from ACIP providing vaccination recommendations. It is NOT a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a policy/guidance document from ACIP providing vaccination recommendations. It is NOT a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet study design criteria.

This is a review article that summarizes data from other trials (mentions 'a large case-controlled trial and two randomized controlled trials' and 'a meta-analysis'). It is NOT itself an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a meta-analysis pooling data from 5 trials. It is NOT itself a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a modeling/projection study about global mortality and burden of disease. It is NOT a randomised controlled trial of influenza vaccination. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a case-control study (explicitly stated in abstract: 'A case-control study was performed on 218 CHD patients'). It is NOT a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet study design criteria.
